title: The Sleeping Portrait
premise: Mara Zhou takes a teaching post in the remote town of Hollowmere, where students vanish one by one and the town's oldest families keep meticulous ledgers of every disappearance. When an excavation crew unearths a stone door sealed from the inside beneath the school, Mara's obsessive documentation becomes the only map of what is happening—and the only thing keeping him visible to whatever counts the living. He discovers the founding families survive by feeding names to something in the well, and that his own name has been entered into the ledger. In the end, Mara burns the ledgers and leads the remaining families out ahead of the final count, but the door, unsealed at last, stands open behind them—suggesting the well refills with whoever forgets to look back.
about_author: Casper Almeida is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in towns too small for maps and too old for comfort. They write horror about institutions, ledgers, and the quiet violence of being counted.

chapters.title: The Longest Bus Route
chapters.summary: Mara Zhou arrives in Hollowmere on a bus with no return schedule, taking the teaching post no one else wanted. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: wary hope, the relief of starting over where nobody knows his failures.

chapters.title: Attendance Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: First day of class; twenty-three students, but the classroom has thirty desks. Mara begins documenting everything in a battered notebook. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional diligence.

chapters.title: The Ledger Keepers
chapters.summary: At a faculty dinner, Mara meets the Voss and Aldery families, who run the town and speak of the school's history in accounting terms. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: charm with teeth under it.

chapters.title: Empty Chair, Full Desk
chapters.summary: A student named Ilsa fails to arrive; her desk is cleared overnight as if she never existed. No one files a report. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: first real dread, the horror of institutional calm.

chapters.title: What the Ground Remembers
chapters.summary: An excavation crew arrives to dig the school's new foundation. Old-timers watch from porches, saying nothing. POV: crew foreman Denny Okafor. Emotional beat: superstitious reluctance among practical men.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two
chapters.summary: Mara cross-references enrollment records going back decades and finds a pattern: classes shrink by exactly one each autumn. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the thrill of a pattern becoming the terror of one.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Brother
chapters.summary: Tomas, Ilsa's brother, tells Mara the family 'gave her up' and begs him not to write it down. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: loyalty strangling truth.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: The crew strikes stone forty feet down: a carved door, its bolts thrown from within. The foreman wants to stop; the Alderys insist they continue. POV: Denny. Emotional beat: awe curdling into violation.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Mayor Voss visits Mara's classroom, compliments his thoroughness, and asks to see his notebook. Mara lies for the first time. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility stops working.

chapters.title: Chalk Dust and Cold Air
chapters.summary: The school's lower hallway breathes cold; students report humming through the floor. One girl draws the door perfectly without ever seeing it. POV: student Wren Aldery. Emotional beat: children knowing more than adults admit.

chapters.title: A History of Subtractions
chapters.summary: In the town archive, Mara finds the founding families' ledgers: names, dates, and a column labeled simply 'PAID.' His own surname appears in a 1911 entry. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past reaching for him personally.

chapters.title: Denny Quits
chapters.summary: The foreman refuses to dig further; that night his equipment is found arranged in a perfect circle around the shaft. POV: Denny. Emotional beat: fear winning over money, and shame over both.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Wren explains the family doctrine: the thing below must be given a number each season or it comes up to count for itself. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terrible matter-of-factness of inherited survival.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Mara confronts Headmistress Voss; she shows him the ledger page bearing his name, entered before he ever applied. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the collapse of his belief he chose this town.

chapters.title: Bargaining With the Dark
chapters.summary: Mara offers himself in exchange for the students; the headmistress laughs—not cruelly, which is worse. The ledger doesn't trade, it accumulates. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: humiliation, then resolve.

chapters.title: The Hum Gets Louder
chapters.summary: The whole town hears it now. Dogs leave. The excavation shaft exhales warm air that smells like the school's chalk. POV: Denny. Emotional beat: collective denial cracking.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren secretly gives Mara the family's true ledger—the original, pre-doctrine record showing the door was sealed to imprison something, not to honor it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: loyalty breaking toward truth.

chapters.title: Autumn Count Eve
chapters.summary: Preparations for the annual 'Founders' Audit,' when the families descend to the door with the year's name. Mara realizes this year's name is his. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: countdown dread.

chapters.title: The Teacher Who Wouldn't Erase
chapters.summary: Mara copies every ledger, hides duplicates in students' backpacks, and teaches them a code phrase. Documentation as evacuation plan. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: purpose replacing panic.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: POV shifts below: Mayor Voss and the elders perform the audit ritual at the sealed door; the bolts begin turning on their own. Emotional beat: ritual confidence meeting something that stopped listening.

chapters.title: It Counts Back
chapters.summary: The door opens inward. Something ascends the shaft counting aloud—names, dates, debts. Three elders don't come back up. POV: Denny, watching from the rim. Emotional beat: cosmic horror made procedural.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: The school seals itself; doors won't open, windows show fog where the town should be. The building is part of the mechanism. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: claustrophobia, betrayal by shelter itself.

chapters.title: The Names It Knows
chapters.summary: The presence speaks through the intercom in the voices of missing students, reciting Mara's notebook entries back to him, errors included. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: being known is worse than being hunted.

chapters.title: Tomas Runs
chapters.summary: Tomas panics and tries to give the presence another name—Wren's—to save himself. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: loyalty's ugliest hour, and immediate shame.

chapters.title: What Wren Paid
chapters.summary: Wren accepts the offered substitution calmly, but Mara refuses to let the ledger balance; he tears out the page bearing her name mid-transaction. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: defiance as love; the rules bending.

chapters.title: The Well Does Not Forgive
chapters.summary: The interrupted count causes the school to convulse; hallways rearrange, classrooms become the archive, the archive becomes the shaft mouth. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: disorientation, stakes made physical.

chapters.title: Ledger Burners
chapters.summary: Mara gathers the surviving students and reveals the plan: the presence is bound to the records—if every copy burns before dawn's final count, it loses its arithmetic. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: desperate hope with a terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Archive Fire
chapters.summary: They burn the town archive; the fire burns wrong, upward and slow, and the smoke spells numbers. Half the ledgers are ash. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the sense of waking something.

chapters.title: Recount
chapters.summary: The presence, wounded by lost records, begins physically counting—doors slamming in sequence, a voice tallying heartbeats. It will finish by dawn regardless. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: the plan failing faster than hope can adjust.

chapters.title: Okafor's Shaft
chapters.summary: Denny returns with blasting equipment: if they can't erase the debt, they can bury the creditor. The group splits—burn above, blast below. POV: Denny. Emotional beat: guilt-driven courage.

chapters.title: Down the Throat
chapters.summary: Mara descends the shaft with the last original ledger, intending to read the founding names aloud—returning the debt to its creditors. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: descent as acceptance.

chapters.title: The First Families' Voices
chapters.summary: Below, Mara finds the missing students alive but hollow-eyed, tending the presence like gardeners. They don't want rescue; they want the counting to mean something. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: horror of consent.

chapters.title: Reading the Roll
chapters.summary: Mara reads the founders' true names from the original ledger; the presence falters, remembering it was once people who refused to be counted. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: revelation—the monster is the first refusal.

chapters.title: The Door From Either Side
chapters.summary: Denny's charges blow the shaft as Mara shoves the students toward the light; the presence screams in every name it ever collected. POV: alternating Mara/Denny. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, noise, collapse.

chapters.title: Above Ground, Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Mara crawls out at the final second; the count reaches his name and finds no ledger to confirm it. Silence. The school stands ordinary and wrong. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: survival that feels like theft.

chapters.title: Getting the Family Out
chapters.summary: Mara loads the surviving students and the defector families onto Denny's trucks before the town wakes; some elders choose to stay with their ledgers. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: exodus grief—loyalty to the living over the dead.

chapters.title: The Town That Stays Behind
chapters.summary: From the ridge, they watch Hollowmere go quiet, windows lighting one by one like a tally. The headmistress waves, serene, still holding her book. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt wearing the mask of victory.

chapters.title: New Attendance Sheet
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in a coastal town, Mara teaches again—smaller class, real desks. He keeps documenting, but now the notebook ends each day with the students' names spoken aloud, freely. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: healing as deliberate remembrance.

chapters.title: The Page That Survived
chapters.summary: Wren finds one ledger page tucked in her backpack—her own name, torn out, preserved. Someone kept a copy. She doesn't tell Mara. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: ambiguity, the seed of sequel dread.

chapters.title: The Door Stands Open
chapters.summary: Final image: far beneath collapsed Hollowmere, the sealed door hangs open, and somewhere a fresh page turns itself, waiting for the next name written carelessly. POV: omniscient. Emotional beat: the price of survival is never paid in full.
